source_text: Nunc de spiritalibus. dico haec quoque, in Christum a creatore promissa ***, sub illa praescriptione, iustissima opinor, qua non alterius credenda sit exhibitio, quam cuius probata fuerit repromissio. pronuntiauit Esaias: prodibit uirga de radice Iesse, et flos [de radice] ascendet de uirga, et requiescet super eum spiritus dei. dehinc species eius enumerat: spiritus sapientiae et intellegentiae, spiritus consilii et ualentiae, spiritus agnitionis et religionis, spiritus eum replebit timoris dei. Christum enim in floris figura ostendit, oriturum ei uirga profecta de radice Iesse, id est uirgine generis Dauid, filii Iesse, in quo Christo consistere haberet tota substantia spiritus, non quasi postea obueutura illi, qui semper spiritus dei fuerit, ante carnem quoque, - ne ex hoc argumenteris prophetiam ad eum Christum pertinere, qui ut homo tantum ex solo censu Dauid postea consecuturus sit dei sui spiritum, — sed quoniam exinde, quo floruisset in carne sumpta ex stirpe Dauid, requiescere in illo haberet omnis operatio gratiae spiritalis et concessare et finem facere, quantum ad Iudaeos; sicut et res ipsa testatur, nihil exinde spirante penes illos spiritu creatoris, ablato a Iudaea sapiente et prudente architecto et consiliario et propheta, ut hoc sit: lex et prophetae usque ad Iohannem. accipe nunc, quomodo et a Christo in caelum recepto charismata obuentura pronuntiarit: ascendit in sublimitatem, id est in caelum; captiuam duxit captiuitatem, id est mortem uel humanam seruitutem; data dedit filiis hominum, id est donatiua, quae charismata dicimus. eleganter 'filiis hominum' ait, non passim (hominibus nos ostendens filios hominum, id est uere hominum, apostolorum. in euangelio enim, inquit, ego uos generaui, et: filii mei, quos parturio rursus, iam nunc et illa promissio spiritus absoluta, facta per Iohelem: in nouissimis temporibus effundam de meo spiritu in omnem carnem, et prophetabunt filii filiaeque eorum, et super seruos et ancillas meas de meo spiritu -effundam. et utique si in nouissimos dies gratiam spiritus creator repromisit, Christus autem spiritalium dispensator in nouissimis diebus apparuit dicente apostolo: at ubi tempus expletum est, misit deus filium suum, et rursus: quia tempus iam in collecto est, apparet et de temporum ultimorum praedicatione hanc gratiam spiritus ad Christum praedicatoris pertinere. compara denique species apostoli et Esaiae. alii, inquit, datur per spiritum sermo sapientiae: statim et Esaias sapientiae spiritum posuit; alii sermo scientiae: hic erit sermo intellegentiae et consilii; alii fides in eodem spiritu: hic erit spiritus religionis et timoris dei; alii donum curationum, alii uirtutum: hic erit ualentiae spiritus; alii prophetia, alii distinctio spirituum, alii genera linguarum, alii interpretatio linguarum: hic erit agnitionis spiritus. uide apostolum et in distributione facienda unius spiritus et in specialitate interpretanda prophetae conspirantem. possum dicere: ipsum quod corporis nostri per multa et diuersa membra unitatem charismatum uariorum compagini adaequauit, eundem et corporis humani et spiritus sancti dominum ostendit, qui merita charismatum noluerit esse in corpore spiritus, quae nec (membrorum) in corpore humano collocauit, qui de dilectione quoque omnibus charismatibus praeponenda apostolum instruxerit principali praecepto quod probauit et Christus: diliges dominum de totis praecordiis et totis uiribus et tota anima et proximum tibi tamquam te. et si quod in lege scriptum esset commemorat in aliis linguis et in aliis labiis locuturum creatorem, cum hac commemoratione charisma linguarum confirmat, nec hic potest uideri alienum charisma creatoris praedicatione confirmasse.
pass_a_gloss: Now about spiritual things, I say these things also, which were promised by the Creator in Christ, under that prescription, which I think is most just, that no other exhibition is to be believed except that whose promise has been proven. Isaiah pronounced: a rod will come out of the root of Jesse, and a flower will ascend from the rod, and the Spirit of God will rest upon him. Then he enumerates the kinds of him: the Spirit of wisdom and intelligence, the Spirit of counsel and strength, the Spirit of knowledge and religion, the Spirit of fear of God will fill him. For Christ is shown in the figure of a flower, to arise from the rod that came out of the root of Jesse, that is, from the virgin of the family of David, the son of Jesse, in whom the whole substance of the Spirit was to consist, not as if it were to come to him afterwards, who always was the Spirit of God, even before the flesh, - lest you argue from this that the prophecy pertains to that Christ who, as a man only, from the sole lineage of David, would afterwards receive the Spirit of his God, - but because from then on, when he had flourished in the flesh taken from the stock of David, all the operation of spiritual grace was to rest in him and to grant and to make an end, as far as the Jews are concerned; just as the fact itself testifies, that from then on nothing of the Spirit of the Creator breathed among them, with the wise and prudent architect and counselor and prophet taken away from Judea, so that this is: the law and the prophets until John. Receive now how he also pronounced that charisms would come from Christ received into heaven: he ascended into the height, that is, into heaven; he led captivity captive, that is, death or human servitude; he gave gifts, that is, donations, which we call charisms. He elegantly says 'to the sons of men', not in general, showing us that the sons of men, that is, the true men, are the apostles. For in the Gospel, he says: I have generated you, and: my sons, whom I am in labor with again, now already and that promise of the Spirit is fulfilled, which was made through Joel: in the last days I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh, and their sons and daughters will prophesy, and upon my servants and handmaids I will pour out my Spirit. And certainly if in the last days the Creator promised the grace of the Spirit, but Christ, the dispenser of spiritual things, appeared in the last days, as the apostle says: but when the time was fulfilled, God sent his Son, and again: because the time is now gathered, it appears that this grace of the Spirit, from the preaching of the last times, pertains to Christ the preacher. Compare finally the kinds of the apostle and Isaiah. He says: to others is given through the Spirit the word of wisdom; immediately Isaiah also placed the Spirit of wisdom; to others the word of knowledge: this will be the word of intelligence and counsel; to others faith in the same Spirit: this will be the Spirit of religion and fear of God; to others the gift of healings, to others of virtues: this will be the Spirit of strength; to others prophecy, to others distinction of spirits, to others kinds of languages, to others interpretation of languages: this will be the Spirit of knowledge. See the apostle and the prophet conspiring in the distribution to be made of one Spirit and in the interpretation of the specialty. I can say: the same one who has adapted the unity of various charisms to the many and diverse members of our body, shows himself to be the Lord of the human body and of the Holy Spirit, who did not want the merits of the charisms to be in the Spirit, which he did not place in the human body, who also instructed the apostle in the principal precept that Christ approved: love the Lord with all your heart and with all your strength and with all your soul and your neighbor as yourself. And if he recalls something written in the law, that the Creator will speak in other languages and in other lips, with this recollection he confirms the charisma of languages, nor can it be seen here that the charisma of the Creator is alien, which he confirmed with his preaching.

pass_b_english: I also say these things about spiritual matters: the promises the Creator made in Christ stand under a rule that seems perfectly just to me — no exhibition is to be believed unless its promise has already been proven. Isaiah declared it: a shoot will spring from the stump of Jesse, a blossom will rise from that shoot, and the Spirit of God will rest upon him (Isaiah 11:1-2). The prophet then lists the Spirit's qualities: the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and might, the Spirit of knowledge and reverence, the Spirit of the fear of the Lord will fill him. He depicts Christ as that blossom, rising from the shoot that issued from Jesse's root — that is, from the virgin of David's line, David the son of Jesse. In this Christ the whole substance of the Spirit was to dwell, not as something that would arrive later — he was always the Spirit of God, even before taking flesh — lest anyone twist the prophecy to mean a Christ who was merely a man descended from David and only afterwards received the Spirit of his God. Rather, from the moment he blossomed in flesh taken from David's stock, every operation of spiritual grace was to rest in him, to be dispensed and to reach its conclusion, as far as the Jews were concerned. The facts themselves testify: once the wise and prudent architect, counselor, and prophet was removed from Judea, nothing of the Creator's Spirit breathed among them any longer, so that the saying was fulfilled: the law and the prophets until John.

Now observe how Isaiah also announced the charisms that would flow from Christ once he was received into heaven: he ascended into the heights, that is, into heaven; he led captivity captive, that is, death or human bondage; he gave gifts to the sons of men, that is, the endowments we call charisms. He says 'to the sons of men' elegantly, not indiscriminately — showing us that the sons of men, the true men, are the apostles. For in the Gospel he says: I have begotten you, and: my children, whom I am in labor with again (Joel 2:28-29). And already that promise of the Spirit made through Joel is fulfilled: in the last days I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; their sons and daughters will prophesy, and on my male and female servants I will pour out my Spirit. Certainly if the Creator promised the grace of the Spirit for the last days, and Christ, the dispenser of spiritual things, appeared in the last days — as the apostle says: when the time had fully come, God sent his Son, and again: the time is now compressed — it follows that this grace of the Spirit, from the preaching of the final times, belongs to Christ the preacher. Compare finally the lists of the apostle and Isaiah. Paul says: to one is given through the Spirit the word of wisdom — immediately Isaiah also placed the Spirit of wisdom; to another the word of knowledge — this will be the word of understanding and counsel; to another faith in the same Spirit — this will be the Spirit of reverence and the fear of God; to another gifts of healing, to another works of power — this will be the Spirit of might; to another prophecy, to another discernment of spirits, to another kinds of tongues, to another interpretation of tongues — this will be the Spirit of knowledge. See how the apostle and the prophet conspire in distributing the one Spirit and in interpreting the specialties. I can say: the same one who adapted the unity of varied charisms to the many and diverse members of our body reveals himself as Lord of both the human body and the Holy Spirit. He did not want the merits of the charisms to reside in the Spirit — he who never placed them in the human body — and he also instructed the apostle in the principal commandment that Christ himself approved: love the Lord with all your heart, with all your strength, and with all your soul, and your neighbor as yourself. And if he recalls something written in the law, that the Creator will speak in other tongues and with other lips, by that very recollection he confirms the charism of tongues; nor can it be shown here that the Creator's charism is alien, when he confirms it by his own preaching.
